name: Intentional correlation — one controller across k credentials

request.issue: cred-spec #22 (talltree 08-29: 'the ZK proof simply needs to prove the same person controls the DIDs') · cred-spec PR #30 §Choosing a scope
request.need: under three correlation scopes, a holder who used `pairwise` identifiers (distinct by definition) or distinct wider-scoped ones, and now wishes to be recognised as the same party across several communities or relationships, needs one proof — and no other case needs any

dish: A verifier learns that the k credentials in front of it — memberships, relationships, personas — name identifiers all controlled by the presenter, and that none is revoked, while learning no identifier the presenter did not choose to show and receiving no handle that recognises the presenter elsewhere.
ingredients: the holder secret s and each identifier's derivation material
the k credentials (VMCs, VRCs, VPCs) — the holder declares per presentation which of their identifiers are shown and which stay hidden behind commitments
non-revocation witnesses for each credential handle
pantry: the identifiers the holder chooses to disclose (possibly none — the proof can be over commitments alone)
transcriptDigest — one transcript for the whole show

method.clause: for each pair (identifier_1, identifier_i), i = 2..k: both open to the same s — k−1 common-control clauses sharing one witness
no credential handle is in the set under rl_root at epoch
the whole show is bound to transcriptDigest

yield: the holder-declared set of credentials shown to share a controller — a per-presentation choice, the disclosure this card exists to make
the identifiers the holder chose to disclose, and no others
doesNotEstablish: that the presenter is one natural person (k credentials, one secret: an agent holding a person's secret satisfies every clause — card 002 under its own declaration establishes uniqueness)
anything about credentials not in the show: intentional correlation is declared per presentation and does not widen any identifier's declared scope
that the communities involved consented to be named together — the disclosure is the holder's
what any of the credentials asserts beyond existence and non-revocation (a VPC's persona content, a VRC's statement) unless disclosed

adversary.claim: no identifier beyond the disclosed set, and no cross-presentation handle: two verifiers shown different subsets cannot join them through this proof
the issuer of any one credential in the show learns nothing about the others from the proof; the revocation-state fetch must not be a per-holder query (card 006 C3)

horizon: earliest of: any shown credential's validity · epoch rollover · the shortest identifier key-validity among the k (card 007)

rejectionCodes: show-not-declared (lint: a credential in the witness set has no disclosure declaration)

substitutions.route: no proof — where the holder deliberately reused one `directed` or `public` identifier across the credentials, the correlation is on their face (WD02 §Choosing a scope)
Groth16 composition: (k−1) × card-007 openings + k non-revocation legs + 1 transcript constraint
substitutions.cost: unmeasured; conjecture linear in k with the 007 and 006 per-leg costs

issuance: as card 007: every identifier that may later be co-proven is, or carries, a ZK-openable commitment to s (X3 applied to identifiers)

spec: cred-spec PR #30 §Choosing a scope (WD02 draft) · Privacy Consideration 2 (intentional correlation via personas)
cred-spec §VPC (Verifiable Persona Credential) — the credential-layer instrument for the same intent
